newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 9.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 9.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Friday and main factors likely to affect trading:

* Market still has a downward bias due to the possibility of higher U.S. interest rates when the Federal Reserve Open Market Committee meets on May 20, Ramon Saulo, analyst at Asiamerit Securities said.
* Despite the prevailing negative sentiment, accumulation on selected blue chip stocks could be seen, Dharmala Securities analyst Elline Salvatierra said.
* Traders said the 2,600 support level may be tested anew.
* On Thursday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index slipped 12.30 points to 2,682.10.
* The Dow Jones ended up 50.97 points on Thursday at 7,136.62.
* The Central Bank raised on Thursday its borrowing rate by 0.25 percentage points on reverse repos of one to six months.
* Seafront Resources Corp said it signed a deal with six local unlisted companies to jointly form a company to develop a 600-hectare plot just north of the capital.
* The APC Group Inc said its board had agreed to transform the company into a holding firm from an oil exploration company.
* JG Summit Holdings said its board had approved a one-for-four stock rights offer.

* The Sugar Regulatory Administration (SRA) chairman Wilson Gamboa told the U.S. Agricultural Attache that the Philippines does not want to export additional sugar to the United States for crop year 1996/1997 (Sept/Aug).
* Philippine raw sugar output from September 1, 1996 to May 4, 1997 totalled 1.671 million tonnes, the SRA said.
* First Philippine Holdings Corp said it would set up a joint venture with construction firm Balfour Beatty Ltd, a civil engineering unit of BICC Plc of the United Kingdom.
* China Banking Corp reported a 31 percent increase in its first quarter net income to 922 million pesos from 704 million pesos registered a year ago.
* Philex Mining Corp said it sold 390 million pesos worth of copper concentrates, gold and silver in March.
* Condominium developer Primetown Property Group Inc said its board had approved a 75 percent stock dividend to be given to shareholders as of March 26.
* United States-based Bechtel Enterprises International Ltd and GE Capital Asia Pacific Ltd have signed a memorandum of agreement to join Ayala Corp in a $600 million railway project, Ayala said.

* Pilipino Telephone Corp share price plunged to a record low on Thursday as brokers slashed their 1997 earnings forecasts for the first despite assurances by the company of a recovery later this year.

* Newspaper Manila Bulletin said President Fidel Ramos assured local officials of Carson City, California of the holding of national elections in May 1998 and his "graduation" on June 30 of the same year.

* Business Daily said the Central Bank is considering alternative measures to minimise local banks' risks arising from the proliferation of foreign currency deposit units (FCDUs) - without having to impose a reserve requirement or a credit extension ceiling on these instruments.

* Newspaper BusinessWorld said the Securities and Exchange Commission will finalise a circular directing the Philippine Stock Exchange to provide a set of rules prohibiting traders from dealing in their own accounts.
* The peso closed lower at 26.368 to the dollar vs 26.366
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was down to 11.3125 percent from 11.5625 percent.
